notes: The diagram shows barrel_shifter_buf ==> barrel_shifter [bs_result], but the RTL never reads bs_result in barrel_shifter; bs_result is read only by the res_o assignment at line 143.
C1 treats the operand and transformed result as one fixed conceptual asset as required by CONCEPTS, although the RTL has separate serial and barrel implementations.

points.reached by: The rs1_i ==> barrel_shifter arrow carries rs1_i into the barrel data path.
points.reason: The operand is present in bs_level and bs_sign, and valid_cmd, the shift controls, and the input data determine the transformed value.

points.reached by: The barrel_shifter ==> barrel_shifter_core arrow carries bs_level and bs_sign into the staged shift logic.
points.reason: The staged barrel values carry the operand-derived data and shamt_i selects which slices are shifted or copied.

points.reached by: The barrel_shifter ==> barrel_shifter_buf and barrel_shifter_core ==> barrel_shifter_buf arrows carry bs_level into the clocked result register.
points.reason: bs_result stores the computed operand result and can be changed by the barrel data path before it is returned.

points.reached by: The rs1_i ==> serial_shifter_core arrow carries rs1_i into shifter.sreg.
points.reason: shifter.sreg stores and repeatedly transforms the operand, so its contents can be observed or altered before completion.

points.reason: shamt_i is loaded into the serial count and therefore determines how many serial shifts occur.

points.reached by: The ctrl_i --> valid_cmd arrow reaches the logic assignment that computes command acceptance.
points.reason: The decoded control fields determine whether a shift command is accepted, so changing them can select the wrong operation or suppress processing.

points.reached by: The valid_cmd ==> barrel_shifter and ctrl_i ==> barrel_shifter arrows reach the barrel control and sign-selection logic.

points.reached by: The serial_shifter_core ==> serial_shifter arrow reaches the completion logic driven by the serial control state.

points.reason: ctrl_i.ir_funct3 directly selects whether res_o is bit-reversed, so altered control changes the returned operation behavior.
